holder.name: Synthetic Holder A
holder._note: Deliberately a corridor holder: Indian citizen, Irish tax resident since 2018-09-01, resident nowhere else. Standalone India/US packs should return EXEMPT for her (she is not Indian- or US-resident/citizen); the India-Ireland corridor pack is the one that should CONFIRM against her, because it looks at citizenship x tax residency together, not either alone. eea_swiss_uk_national: false for the same reason she needed to register at all: an Indian citizen is not an EEA, Swiss or UK national, so the Irish IRP pack (domains/ireland-irp.yaml) is in scope for her too — a second, non-tax domain pack confirming against the same holder, on a fact this register already carried.

holdings._note: Acceptance-criterion holding: 2019-03-14 acquisition -> next 8-year deemed disposal is 2027-03-14.
Deliberately unaffected: held under 8 years, no deemed disposal has yet arisen.
Deliberately unaffected: instrument type is outside Section 4.1 scope -> COMPASS returns EXEMPT.

Not a financial asset -- the ireland-irp.yaml domain pack (a non-tax, non-Finance sector) treats an immigration permission as a 'holding' in exactly the same generic register shape as an offshore fund or an equity position, proving the register schema is domain-agnostic too. irp_registration_due_date is precomputed here as her 2018-09-01 arrival (tax_residency_since) + 90 days = 2018-11-30, for the one-time DT-IRP-01 trigger. irp_expiry_date is the current permission's actual expiry -- a real fact, not derived from acquisition_date by assuming a fixed term (IRP terms vary and ISD guidance never states one) -- deliberately close to today (2026-09-10) so the demo surfaces a live, near-term renewal deadline rather than a dormant one; acquisition_date (2025-09-15) is kept as the current permission's grant/last-renewal date for record-keeping, but DT-IRP-02 triggers off irp_expiry_date, not off an assumed annual cycle from acquisition_date.
